newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX opens bourse higher, aims for 2,800 pts.
newsitem.headline: German DAX opens bourse higher, aims for 2,800 pts.

text.p: German shares opened bourse dealings higher on Monday, with dealers saying the crucial 2,800 point level was in sight for the DAX index of 30 leading shares this week.
Dealers said both chart technical and fundamental factors supported another attempt at the level, which was breached 10 days ago in post-bourse computer trade but not maintained last week.
They said gains in newly-floated Deutsche Telekom shares and a stronger dollar were supporting the market, along with strength on other foreign stock exchanges.
The DAX index was up almost one percent, or 26.30 points at 2,789.99 by 1034 GMT.
Shares in telecommunications giant Telekom gained over two percent, or 73 pfennigs to 32.75 marks, with dealers saying initial speculative profit taking on the stock had come to an end.
Stocks in the export-oriented chemicals and car sectors were supported by the firmer dollar, which was up nearly a pfennig on its Friday closing level above 1.51 marks.
Meanwhile, shares in Fresenius Medical Care were up 1.20 marks at 139.80 marks, after new preference shares in the dialysis group were issued at 125 marks each.
There was little market reaction to the latest state consumer price index reports out of Hesse and Bavaria.
North Rhein-Westphalia is the last of the states that make up preliminary west German CPI and is due to report data later on Monday.
